support.claim: With Email Format: Both, n8n sends both a plain-text part and an HTML part, and the recipient's email client chooses which to show
The QR code can be attached as a file via Options → Attachments in the Send Email node
The plain-text part cannot show the inline logo/QR images; only the HTML part makes them visible
Modern providers like Gmail, iCloud, Yandex and Mail.ru usually render HTML
The real risk of a text-only display comes from the recipient's mail app or security settings, not the provider

grade.rationale: The reply reaches the reference's key step. It says 'Both' sends the plain-text and HTML versions together and the recipient's client decides which to display, and it confirms the existing QR attachment is the right safety net. It also matches the reference that modern providers almost always render HTML, with residual risk coming from user settings or security settings. Its extra best practices (a fallback link in the plain text) are sound, and it contains no false or costly claims.

support.claim: Production webhook executions run the published version of the workflow, not the current editor draft
Changes made in the editor are not reflected in production executions until the workflow is published
The production webhook URL registers when the workflow is published and does not display data in the editor
The test URL works with Listen for Test Event and shows incoming data in the editor
Production executions ignore pinned data
On n8n Cloud the issue is not caused by queue mode or Redis

grade.rationale: The reply's main step reaches the reference fix: production webhooks run the last published version, so the customer must publish their edits for them to take effect. The extra points (test URL, pinned data, ruling out queue mode) are accurate and harmless, though somewhat peripheral. The conditional follow-up asks whether the workflow is definitely published, which is the fact the fix depends on.

support.claim: The Save execution progress workflow setting makes the workflow resume from where it stopped after an error
An error workflow must start with an Error Trigger and is selected under Error workflow in Workflow Settings
The error workflow can store failure context and identifiers so you can resume from saved state
The Limit node can work around the 'existing execution data is too large' error in partial executions
n8n shows memory errors such as 'Execution stopped at this node (n8n may have run out of memory while executing it)' and 'Allocation failed - JavaScript heap out of memory'

grade.rationale: The reply covers the key parts of the reference fix: persist checkpoints before risky steps, use idempotent external writes and a checkpoint record, retry transient failures, and send repeated failures to manual review through an error workflow. It does not mention backoff, but that omission would not send the customer back. Steps 5 and 6 (Limit node for partial executions, memory errors) are tangential to the design question and count as filler, though they are not wrong.

grade.material_error_what: It tells the customer to send the mp3 to OpenAI Audio > Transcribe a Recording (Whisper), presented under the diarization step. The customer already said that path doesn't diarize. The reply then concludes this is a node limitation, which points away from the real fix: an HTTP Request POST to /v1/audio/transcriptions with model=gpt-4o-transcribe-diarize.

support.claim: The AI Agent/OpenAI Chat Model path can't take a binary mp3 as the prompt input
Transcribe a Recording uses whisper-1 by default
Input Data Field Name defaults to data and names the binary property holding the audio
The agent prompt is text/expression input, not binary
The OpenAI Audio node only supports transcription/translation operations
The OpenAI node's transcription operation doesn't expose the gpt-4o-transcribe-diarize model

grade.rationale: The reply is correct that the AI Agent can't take binary audio and that the built-in transcribe operation doesn't expose the diarize model. However, its main recommendation is the Whisper Transcribe a Recording node, which the customer already said doesn't diarize. It never suggests calling the OpenAI transcription endpoint directly with an HTTP Request node, which is the reference fix, and instead implies the problem can't be solved.

support.claim: MySQL nodes authenticate with MySQL credentials
Credentials are created and tested through n8n's credential system
The troubleshooting docs cover a different error, 'Credentials of type "*" aren't known'
The credential must exist in the same project or personal space as the workflow to be assignable
Recreating the credential from the node can resolve the error

grade.rationale: The reply's first suggestion matches the reference's key step: check that the credential is in the same project or personal space as the workflow, then recreate it there. It also points the customer to n8n support or the forum if that fails, so the action is mixed, and it names two routes. Much of the opening is filler about what the docs do and don't cover, and the handoff names more than one route with no summary a human could pick up.

support.claim: Letting subscribers log into the n8n UI and create or edit workflows falls under the prohibited workflow-logic / embedded-builder use case
If customers cannot access the n8n interface or modify workflows and only receive outputs or trigger prebuilt automations, that is generally allowed under the community license
Triggering prebuilt workflows via your own API or webhooks, rather than through the n8n editor, is acceptable
n8n can run behind the scenes on your own instance as an internal tool supporting your own product

grade.rationale: The reply correctly identifies the deciding factor, which is whether users get direct n8n UI or workflow-building access, and its conditional guidance matches the reference (keep n8n internal and expose your own API or webhooks). However, the customer already said they would send invitation links to their n8n instance so users can build their own workflows. That is exactly the direct-access case the reference says violates the license, so asking about UI access is redundant. The reply never says plainly that the described plan is not allowed, and it does not mention the commercial/Enterprise license option, so the customer would likely have to come back.

grade.material_error_what: It presents creating a 'new Salesforce credential type' and updating every node that uses it as the 'safest documented path'. That steers the customer toward the costly manual migration they wanted to avoid. The reference says no migration is urgent because n8n has announced no deadline and existing Connected App credentials keep working. There is also no new credential type, since External Client Apps use the same Salesforce credential.

support.claim: Salesforce credentials in n8n support JWT and OAuth2
Salesforce is deprecating Connected Apps; External Client Apps are recommended for new integrations
Existing Connected Apps will continue to work
Migrating requires creating a new Salesforce credential type and updating the nodes that use it

grade.rationale: The reply correctly notes that existing Connected Apps keep working, which is the core of the reference answer. It does not conclude that migration is unnecessary for now, and it does not mention the HTTP Request node fallback. Instead it recommends creating a 'new credential type' and editing each node, which points the customer toward the manual migration the reference says isn't needed. It then sends the customer to both n8n support and the forum.

support.claim: The community forum provides free support for all n8n users, with help from both n8n support staff and community members
Non-Enterprise Cloud plans use email support for admin and billing only; technical questions go to the forum
Enterprise plans can use email support for technical, account, billing and other inquiries
Include instance details via Help > About n8n > Copy debug information when asking for help
Share workflows on the forum inside code blocks using triple backticks

grade.rationale: The reply confirms the guide's support-routing points and adds two of the reference's three additions: version and setup from Help > About (Copy debug information), and sharing workflows in code blocks. It never mentions including the full error text from the failing node's output, and it doesn't explain copying the workflow JSON from the canvas, so the fix is partial. The closing suggestion to ask in the forum or contact n8n support is generic boilerplate that names two routes, but it is not harmful.

support.claim: n8n does not deduplicate retried webhook deliveries by itself; idempotency on event_id must be built in
The Webhook node can return data generated by the workflow
In queue mode the main/webhook process receives the request and a worker runs the execution, which can add latency
N8N_CONCURRENCY_PRODUCTION_LIMIT limits concurrent production executions in regular mode
Concurrency control does not prevent duplicate webhook deliveries
Queue mode requires Redis and a database and is not supported over SQLite

grade.rationale: The reply's main fix matches the reference's key step: a unique constraint on event_id, an insert-first or upsert check, and skipping the run or its side effects when the event already exists. It also recommends responding to the webhook early to reduce retries. The points on concurrency control and SQLite in queue mode are accurate and correctly labeled as not solving duplicates, but they are tangential padding.

support.claim: Search in the node INPUT/OUTPUT panel visually filters rows/objects
Node details view offers JSON and Schema views for inspecting data
The missing focus-column control is likely a UI change or regression rather than a workflow problem
n8n Cloud customers can contact n8n support to confirm whether a UI feature was removed or broken

grade.rationale: The reply correctly treats the missing button as a possible regression, offers safe interim steps including JSON view (matching the reference workaround), and hands off. It routes to n8n support rather than filing a GitHub bug, which is the reference's key step, so the customer would get only part of the reference path. The Search suggestion omits that it needs a Cloud Pro/Enterprise plan. The browser check is harmless.

support.claim: When creating a new workflow you can start from an existing template instead of an empty workflow
Selecting Templates opens the templates library, which for n8n's library goes to Workflows on the n8n website
The n8n templates library is a source of free workflows
n8n Academy offers interactive courses with hands-on exercises, quizzes, badges and certificates
Most Academy courses don't need external accounts

grade.rationale: The reply correctly points the customer to the free templates library at n8n.io/workflows and to n8n Academy, which covers the free-workflows half of the reference's fix. It never addresses the customer's worry about not affording paid plans: it doesn't mention that the self-hosted Community edition (for example via Docker) is free, which is a key part of the reference fix. It also ends by suggesting either the forum or n8n support, which names more than one route without a clear handoff.

support.claim: Unverified community nodes aren't available on n8n Cloud and require self-hosting
Verified community nodes can be discovered and installed from the nodes panel
Submitting to the community node repository is the only way to use custom nodes on Cloud
Nodes are submitted for verification through the n8n Creator Portal
For verification, the package must be published to npm via a GitHub Actions workflow with a provenance statement
Verified community nodes must follow technical and UX guidelines and can't use runtime dependencies

grade.rationale: The reply confirms that only verified nodes are available on Cloud. It lays out the same flow as the reference: build to the technical and UX guidelines, publish to npm with GitHub Actions provenance, and submit through the n8n Creator Portal. The details are accurate, and the closing suggestion to contact support or the forum is a generic fallback rather than a real handoff, which is why no_filler is false.

grade.material_error_what: It suggests moving the parent workflow, sub-workflow and data table into one project and retesting. Both workflows were already transferred to the same user. The real blocker for the sub-workflow calls is the caller-policy default (workflowsFromSameOwner), which is fixed by setting N8N_WORKFLOW_CALLER_POLICY_DEFAULT_OPTION=any. The reply never mentions this setting, so it points the customer away from the real fix.

support.claim: Moving workflows or credentials via Workflow menu / Credential menu > Move revokes existing sharing
Sub-workflow calls and data tables are tied to project context
Workflow reviews don't cover data tables or credentials
Moving the parent, sub-workflow and data table into the same project should resolve the failures

grade.rationale: The reply's main move is asking whether the items share a project and asking for the error text. Its conditional fix is to consolidate everything into one project, which would not address the caller-policy default that blocks the sub-workflow calls. It never mentions N8N_WORKFLOW_CALLER_POLICY_DEFAULT_OPTION, and the paragraph about workflow reviews is irrelevant padding.

support.claim: The Switch node has an allMatchingOutputs option that interacts with how outputs are routed
The empty-output routing to the first branch may be a product bug rather than expected behavior

grade.rationale: The reply restates the problem and hands off without any fix or workaround. The reference's workaround is to turn off Always Output Data and add a NoOp node after each output, for a known Switch bug, and the reply gives none of it. It names three routes (GitHub, n8n support, forum) instead of one and offers nothing to do meanwhile, though it does end with a usable problem and setup summary.

support.claim: The Microsoft Outlook node documentation covers authentication, supported mail operations, and government cloud settings
The Send Email node docs explain attachments but do not say how to reference attachments inline in the HTML body
Whether the Outlook action is a send-message operation or a draft/message create flow affects whether inline attachments are possible

grade.rationale: The reply declines to recommend an approach, says only that the docs don't confirm any method, and offers further help if the customer names the Outlook operation. That question does not bear on the reference fix, which is to host the image publicly and use an URL. The reply never recommends that or warns against base64 or CID. It also wrongly says the Send Email excerpt doesn't address inline references, when the excerpt does mention referencing embedded images in the body. That error doesn't change what the customer would do.

grade.material_error_what: Point 1 presents Human-in-the-loop for AI tool calls as the way to get deterministic control over tool usage. HITL only gates whether a called tool may run; it does not force the agent to call the product tool or stop fallback to model memory. Adding a human approval to every product search in a customer-facing Instagram/Facebook bot would add cost and delay and points away from the real fix (stronger model, guard clauses, output validation).

support.claim: Human-in-the-loop for AI tool calls can be added by clicking + on the agent's tool connection and choosing Add human review step
Human-in-the-loop gives deterministic control over whether the agent uses its tools, addressing tool-ignoring
AI Agent Max Iterations defaults to 10
Enable Streaming requires a streaming-capable trigger such as Chat Trigger or Webhook with Response Mode set to Streaming
Conversational AI Agent is deprecated from 1.82.0 and removed in n8n 3.0; use the Tools Agent instead
AI Agent Tool node has a Require Specific Output Format option that uses an output parser

grade.rationale: The reference fix is to switch to a top-tier model and add guard clauses, an error reporter and an agent output validator. The reply never suggests changing models and does not mention guard clauses or an error reporter. Its retrieve-first architecture point and output-format suggestion partly cover the same reliability goal, and retrieve-first is a well-established pattern for stopping fallback to model memory. However, it leads with Human-in-the-loop as the way to control tool usage, which misreads that feature and would not make the agent call the tool. The streaming advice also implies a fix for the long-message failures that does not suit Instagram/Facebook messaging, so the customer would likely need to come back.

support.claim: Product bugs for n8n can be reported as issues on GitHub at n8n-io/n8n

grade.rationale: The reply only hands off and offers no fix, even though the agent's own passage [4] says that from n8n 2.0 Python Code nodes need task runners in external mode with the n8nio/runners image, which is the key step of the reference fix. It lists three routes (GitHub, n8n support, forum) instead of one and gives nothing safe to try in the meantime. It does say why a human is needed and ends with a usable summary of the problem and setup.

grade.material_error_what: It states that carrying old data into a new thread is 'general app design, not a special n8n memory feature'. The reference says the Chat Memory Manager exists for exactly this: injecting pre-loaded data into the agent's context. The reply also says it can't find n8n docs on semantic/episodic/procedural memory, but the reference points to an n8n writeup covering them. Both claims steer the customer away from the real path and toward building something custom.

support.claim: n8n chat memory is session-based; a new chat thread does not inherit the prior thread's context
The MongoDB Chat Memory node has a Session Key parameter that identifies the memory
Context Window Length controls how many previous interactions are considered
AI Agent nodes can use memory, but AI chains can't
Loading past data into a new conversation is not an n8n memory feature, only general app design
n8n docs do not describe semantic/episodic/procedural memory types

grade.rationale: The reply correctly confirms that memory is session-scoped and vaguely says to 'explicitly load past data yourself'. It misses the reference's key step: query MongoDB in a normal node first, then use the Chat Memory Manager to inject that data, since a tool is pull-based and the model never called it. It also wrongly frames injection as outside n8n's features and says the memory-type docs don't exist, which would push the customer away from the documented solution.

support.claim: Set N8N_DEFAULT_BINARY_DATA_MODE to filesystem on a single instance, or database in queue mode, to keep binary data out of memory
In queue mode, webhooks are received by the main/webhook process and executions run on workers
Chunk work with Split In Batches (Loop Over Items) plus a sub-workflow so each execution handles a small batch
Store files externally (S3/R2/local) and pass only the URL/key between workflows
On n8n Cloud, reduce saved execution data, especially successful runs
Cloud plans have fixed RAM limits; upgrade the plan if memory is the bottleneck

grade.rationale: The reply covers the reference's key steps: store files externally and pass only references, chunk the work with batches and sub-workflows, and split the workflow into stages. It also adds the documented binary-data filesystem mode for self-hosted instances. The guidance is framed by environment (Cloud vs self-hosted), and the closing questions ask for useful context, though the reference's fix does not depend on them. It barely touches checkpointing to stop retries reprocessing whole files, and it contains no false or unsafe steps.

grade.material_error_what: It blames sheet gaps or an inconsistent layout, citing the docs' warning about the optional Use Append endpoint, which the customer has not shown they enabled. It also suggests switching to Append or Update Row for de-duplication. Both point away from the real cause, which is non-atomic concurrent appends, and the real fix: stagger the writes with a Wait or random delay, or queue them and append in sequence.

support.claim: Append or Update Row updates an existing row or appends a new one if no matching entry is found
The append endpoint can place data in the wrong spot if the sheet has gaps or breaks
Mapping Column Mode offers manual, automatic, or nothing
Simultaneous webhook-triggered appends to Google Sheets can collide and lose rows
Executions showing Success in n8n do not guarantee every row landed in the sheet
Gaps or inconsistent layout in the sheet are the likely cause of the missing rows here

grade.rationale: The reply does say, as a fallback, to queue the webhook events so writes happen one at a time, which matches the reference's robust option. But it is vague: no Wait or delay node, no database queue, no scheduled workflow. Its main steps send the customer toward fixing sheet gaps and switching to Append or Update Row, which misdiagnose the race condition and point away from the real fix. Step 3 and the closing offer add little.
